ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure is an experimental data table, with column headings Experiment, [A] (M), [B] (M), Initial Rate of Formation of C (mol/L-sec). The three rows of data are respectively: Experiment 1, [A]=0.20 M, [B]=0.10 M, initial rate=3×10^-2; Experiment 2, [A]=0.20 M, [B]=0.20 M, initial rate=6×10^-2; Experiment 3, [A]=0.40 M, [B]=0.20 M, initial rate=6×10^-2. Reasoning: Comparing Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, [A] remains unchanged at 0.20 M, [B] doubles from 0.10 M to 0.20 M, and the rate also doubles from 3×10^-2 to 6×10^-2, so it is first order with respect to B. Comparing Experiment 2 and Experiment 3, [B] remains unchanged at 0.20 M, [A] doubles from 0.20 M to 0.40 M, but the rate remains unchanged at 6×10^-2, so it is zero order with respect to A. Therefore the rate law is Rate = k[A]^0[B]^1 = k[B].

raw_record.question_text: Given a reaction A+B → C. Based on the following experimental data, what is the rate law for the hypothetical reaction given above?

method.method_draft: First describe the image table and extract the three experiment rows. Compare experiments 1 and 2: [A] stays 0.20 M, [B] doubles from 0.10 to 0.20 M, and the rate doubles from 3×10^-2 to 6×10^-2, so the reaction is first order in B. Compare experiments 2 and 3: [B] stays 0.20 M, [A] doubles from 0.20 to 0.40 M, and the rate stays 6×10^-2, so the reaction is zero order in A. Combine these orders in Rate = k[A]^0[B]^1 to get Rate = k[B].
